summary: Amazon's DSP model creates political/regulatory risk that Amazon should proactively address — long-term shareholder view
summary_extended: Baker, a self-described long-term Amazon shareholder with a 'very big position' he continues to increase annually, argues that Amazon has become 'too clever' with its Delivery Service Partner (DSP) model, which classifies delivery drivers as independent contractors rather than employees. He predicts that New Jersey and New York will prevail in their ongoing lawsuits against Amazon over driver classification, and that this labor issue will become a potent political flashpoint for democratic socialists in the 2026 midterms and 2028 presidential cycle. Speaking from the perspective of a long-term shareholder rather than making a near-term buy/sell call, Baker recommends Amazon proactively convert its core DSP drivers to full employees to get ahead of the regulatory and political risk before it is forced to do so under less favorable conditions. The investment implication is a risk management flag on AMZN — not a bearish call, but a warning that failure to act could result in material legal liability, reputational damage, and forced structural change at a politically inopportune moment.
